title: Grafting React UI package foundation
objective: Create one reusable @grafting/ui React package organized by Atomic Design, isolate Ant Design behind Grafting-owned component contracts, provide the first need-driven table and entity presentation components, and record the evaluated UI composition decisions without integrating the package into Architecture Studio yet.
validations: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile: passed for all six pnpm workspace projects
pnpm --filter @grafting/ui check/build: strict TypeScript declaration and JavaScript builds passed
pnpm exec nx run ui:test: 4/4 server-rendered behavior contracts passed without warnings
pnpm exec nx run ui:api-check: 5 shared API-tool tests passed; the tracked baseline matched and no antd module leaked
pnpm audit --prod: no known vulnerabilities found
pnpm docs:check: repo map, artifact manifest, Graph IR, Rust API, and x6-canvas API drift checks passed; Graph IR contains 49 nodes and 47 edges
Nx project inspection: ui discovered with check, build, test, api-check, Graph IR, and public-API metadata
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m automation.coordination --root .: passed with 23 task records before completion
package/task JSON parsing and git diff --check: passed
CI workflow received the exact ui check/test/api-check targets; a GitHub Actions runner and local YAML parser were unavailable for an end-to-end workflow execution
risks: Atomic Design folders must be created only for implemented components, not as an empty future tree.
Ant Design types and configuration objects must remain private to the package boundary.
TanStack Table must not be combined redundantly with Ant Design Table or installed before a concrete need justifies replacing the internal table engine.
The UI package is React-specific by design, but its component inputs and behavior use Grafting vocabulary rather than Ant Design contracts.
This foundation is not integrated into Architecture Studio yet; a separately claimed task must add the React/X6 shape and visual browser acceptance.
Ant Design's bundle contribution has not been measured in a real consuming application yet; the first integration should record it before adding broader component imports.
